refutation.item: studies/rlneurons/results/reward5/readout.json (commit 93c0c1c, 2026-11-14 19:31, before the round spec c1b8486), cell code30_cue, the run behind result-edceef
refutation.note: The theory says that at T 1.0 on MATH-500 Code 3.0's runaway mode 'drives its longest problems to the 16,384 cap', and its GPU prediction expects about 30 cap hits on the 125 Q4 problems (refuted below 15). The stored Code 3.0 cue cell is the same job (abaybektursun-1114-182730-9523; axis manifest arm code30_cue points to it) whose 0/1 vectors the four offline tests scored. It has 5 cap hits on all 500 problems: fewer than the cued base (27) and Code 3.1 cue (7). Code 3.0 has 89 wrong answers, and at most 5 of them can be cap hits. So the 31-problem Q4 lead of Code 3.1 (D_q = [-6, 3, 11, 31]) and the -11.25 Q4 deficit to the base cannot come mostly from cap hits. The theory's scope names exactly this cell (MATH-500, cue, T 1.0, cap 16,384, one sample), so it does not exclude it. The theory listed the low mean token count (3,069) as a conflict but never checked the stored cap count. Its 13 rule-A loops and 5 word-salad tails show some degeneration, but it ends before the cap. after.jsonl has no item that measures Code 3.0 cap hits; result-faf15a and knowledge-90431f mention Code 3.0 and do not bear on this. I also read result-edceef with its audit comments, and the board list of 60 new items.

wins_judgement: All four offline predictions fell inside their intervals, for a total of +5.76 nats. The largest gain is p3 (+2.62): Code 3.1 minus Code 3.0 on the short half was measured at -3, where the readers expected +10 to +15. Next are p1 (+1.75; Q4 share 0.79, readers 0.45) and p4 (+0.75), then p2 (+0.64). All four are a quartile pattern: the 3.0-vs-3.1 gap is confined to long, hard problems, and Code 3.0 is at or above the base on short ones. Any length- or difficulty-confined failure gives this pattern, whether early commit, loops below the cap, or wrong finished answers. The cap-hit mechanism is not needed for any of the four numbers, and the stored cap count (5/500) shows it did not produce them. The readers' miss on p3 reflects their prior that Code 3.0 lacks the skill everywhere. The theory's correct claim, that the difference is length-confined and not a missing skill, earned that gain. Its causal story, truncation masking leading to cap hits, earned none. Test script p1 implements its recipe as written: the code_cue and code30_cue arms, quartiles by t2_generated_tokens with ties by problem_index, missing rows as 0, and D_4/D with the D<=0 rule.
rival: The duel state is beats rival: +8.75 nats over 5 tests, 3 of them separating. I read the turn-2 duel script p3; it implements the rival's recipe as written: Q4 ranks 376-500, subset E where base samples 0 and 1 are both right, Code 3.0 mean minus the mean of base samples 2 and 3, and a uniqueness check on the Code 3.0 arm. The rival (a commit-and-stop policy whose deficit follows base difficulty) explains the four offline numbers as well as the theory does. The tests that separate the two are the duel's turn-2 k3 and k4. On Q4 problems the base reliably solves, Code 3.0 trails the held-out base by 0.18 (theory -0.08 [-0.17, 0.01], rival -0.02; the result is outside both intervals but nearer the theory). Only 0.41 of the Q4 deficit lies on base-hard problems (rival 1.0 [0.62, 1.4]). So the failure is not purely difficulty-driven, which goes against the rival. But with 5 cap hits in the cell, those base-easy losses are not cap hits either: they are finished wrong answers or sub-cap degenerations. The duel picked the theory's 'strikes long problems regardless of difficulty' prediction, not its cap mechanism.

novelty.nearest: UloRL (Du et al., 2025), section 3.5: 'our experiments reveal that overlong filtering leads to a rapid increase in the output length', so it treats overlong samples as reward 0. Olmo 3 (2512.13961), appendix A.6.4, says 3.1 stopped masking truncated sequences and that completion lengths were higher with masking.
novelty.difference: Those papers report that masking truncated rollouts inflates output length during training. The theory adds that, in Olmo-3 Code 3.0, the inflation shows up at evaluation as cap hits confined to the longest MATH-500 quartile and cancels the cross-domain math gain there. That addition is the part the stored data contradicts.

import_carries_gain.which: The DAPO import (2503.14476, overlong filtering masks truncated samples) supplies only the causal story: masking leads to an unsuppressed runaway mode, which leads to cap hits. None of the winning numbers (p1-p4, duel k3/k4) depends on cap hits or on masking. They test only where along the length axis the 3.0-vs-3.1 gap lies, and the stored cap count of 5/500 shows the imported mechanism is not what produced them.

verdict: refuted: duel state beats rival and its offline quartile predictions hold, but its stated mechanism (Code 3.0's longest MATH-500 problems driven to the 16,384 cap at T 1.0) is contradicted by the scored cell itself, which has 5 cap hits on 500 problems (base 27, Code 3.1 7), so the length-confined deficit it predicted comes from something other than cap hits.
